Finnish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Internationalism (see English agony), ultimately from Ancient Greek ἀγωνία (agōnía).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈɑɡoniɑ/, [ˈɑ̝ɡo̞ˌniɑ̝]
  • Rhymes: -iɑ
  • Syllabification(key): a‧go‧ni‧a
  • Hyphenation(key): ago‧nia

Noun

[edit]

agonia

  1. agony, death struggle
    Synonym: kuolinkamppailu

Indonesian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἀγωνία (agōnía, “emulation, competition, struggle”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Standard Indonesian) IPA(key): /aɡoˈnia/ [a.ɡoˈni.a]
  • Rhymes: -a
  • Syllabification: a‧go‧ni‧a

Noun

[edit]

agonia (plural agonia-agonia)

  1. agony, extreme pain
  2. agony, violent contest or striving
  3. agon

Adjective

[edit]

agonia (comparative lebih agonia, superlative paling agonia)

  1. agonal, relating to an agon
  2. agonal, relating to the time before death

Further reading

[edit]
  • “agonia”, in Kamus Besar Bahasa Indonesia [Great Dictionary of the Indonesian Language] (in Indonesian), Jakarta: Agency for Language Development and Cultivation – Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology of the Republic of Indonesia, 2016

Noun

agonia f (plural agonie)

  1. agony

Polish

[edit]
Polish Wikipedia has an article on:
agonia
Wikipedia pl

Etymology

[edit]

Internationalism; compare English agony. Possible borrowed from German Agonie or from French agonie,[1][2] ultimately from Ancient Greek ἀγωνία (agōnía, “emulation, competition, struggle”), from ἀγών (agṓn, “contest”). First attested in 1722.[3][4]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /aˈɡɔɲ.ja/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɔɲja
  • Syllabification: a‧gon‧ia

Noun

[edit]

agonia f

  1. agony (struggle that precedes death)

Declension

[edit]
Declension of agonia
singular plural
nominative agonia agonie
genitive agonii agonii
dative agonii agoniom
accusative agonię agonie
instrumental agonią agoniami
locative agonii agoniach
vocative agonio agonie

[edit]
adjectives
  • agonalny
  • agoniczny

[edit]
adjective
  • agonistyczny
nouns
  • agon
  • agonista
  • agonistyka

Collocations

[edit]
Collocations
  • bliski agonii ― close to agony
  • powolna agonia ― slow agony
  • przedśmiertna agonia ― dying agony
  • bolesna agonia ― painful agony
  • długa agonia ― long agony
  • straszliwa agonia ― excruciating agony
  • długotrwała agonia ― lengthy agony
  • wieczna agonia ― eternal agony
  • ludzka agonia ― human agony
  • stan agonii ― a state of agony
  • opis agonii ― a description of (someone's) agony
  • zapis agonii ― a record/transcript of (someone's) agony
  • świadek agonii ― a witness to (someone's) agony
  • męka agonii ― the ordeal of agony
  • faza agonii ― the phase of agony
  • początek agonii ― the beginning of agony
  • moment/chwila agonii ― a moment of agony
  • czas agonii ― the time of agony
  • okres agonii ― the period of agony
  • godzina agonii ― an hour of agony
  • dzień agonii ― a day of agony
  • proces agonii ― a process of agony
  • przedłużać/przedłużyć ― to prolong agony
  • przeciągać agonię ― to draw out agony
  • przyspieszyć/przyśpieszyć agonię ― to accelerate/speed up/hasten agony
  • przeżywać agonię ― to experience/live through/go through agony
  • oznaczać agonię ― to mean agony
  • towarzyszyć agonii ― to accompany agony
  • agonia trwa/potrwa ― agony lasts/will last (a certaim amount of time)

Portuguese

[edit]
Portuguese Wikipedia has an article on:
agonia
Wikipedia pt

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Ecclesiastical Latin agonia, from Ancient Greek ἀγωνία (agōnía, “emulation, competition, struggle”), from ἀγών (agṓn, “contest”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /a.ɡoˈni.ɐ/, /a.ɡuˈni.ɐ/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /a.ɡoˈni.ɐ/, /a.ɡuˈni.ɐ/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /a.ɡoˈni.a/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ɐ.ɡuˈni.ɐ/ [ɐ.ɣuˈni.ɐ]

  • Hyphenation: a‧go‧ni‧a

Noun

[edit]

agonia f (plural agonias)

  1. agony (violent contest or striving)
  2. (uncountable) the state of agony
  3. agony (symptom)

Synonyms

[edit]
  • ânsia, angústia, aflição, sofrimento, agoniação

Related terms

[edit]
  • agoniar, agonizar, agônico, agoniado, agonizante

Further reading

[edit]
  • “agonia”, in Dicionário Aulete Digital (in Portuguese), Rio de Janeiro: Lexikon Editora Digital, 2008–2026
  • “agonia”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026
